researchPolicy: Never write retrieved Fathers' words from model paraphrase. Modern questions are navigation labels, not patristic quotations. English source anchors are short checks against scanned original-work paragraphs, and linked Catena source pointers are existing records. No ingestion of CCEL web-page text or later digital editorial apparatus as automatically reusable content.

editionBases.work: St Augustine: Sermon on the Mount; Harmony of the Gospels; Homilies

rows.editorialQuestion: How can Mark describe the demoniac as torn while Luke says he was unhurt?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: For how could the unclean spirit have been
rows.contextGuard: distinguishes being thrown or tormented from lasting bodily injury

rows.editorialQuestion: Why does Matthew name Jeremiah where the thirty pieces appear in Zechariah?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: How, then, is the matter to be explained
rows.contextGuard: Augustine entertains a textual-variant possibility but rejects simply deleting Jeremiah; preserve multiple proposed reasons

rows.editorialQuestion: Did Jesus bear his cross or did Simon of Cyrene bear it?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: Jesus was carrying the cross Himself as He went forth
rows.contextGuard: Augustine gives successive carrying; translator footnote offers a different possibility, do not attribute editor's footnote to Augustine

rows.editorialQuestion: How can Mark's third hour be reconciled with John's sixth hour?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: how could He have been crucified at the third hour
rows.contextGuard: Augustine's suggested allocation of third/sixth hours is a harmonizing interpretation, not a separately attested chronology

rows.editorialQuestion: How can both thieves revile Christ if Luke says only one did?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: The question then is, how we can reconcile
rows.contextGuard: Existing Catena pointer; distinguish Augustine's plural-for-singular explanation from Theophylact's later-repentance possibility

rows.editorialQuestion: Was the Resurrection angel outside the tomb or inside on the right?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: It is possible, however, that some difficulty may be felt
rows.contextGuard: Augustine presents alternatives including two angels versus different spatial descriptions; do not collapse alternatives into historical certainty

rows.editorialQuestion: How can Mark say the women told no one if Matthew says they ran to tell the disciples?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: It may also be asked how it is that Mark says
rows.contextGuard: must inspect the complete next context before choosing a single answer; location anchor confirmed

rows.editorialQuestion: How are three days and three nights reckoned for the Resurrection?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: the part is dealt with as the whole
rows.contextGuard: inclusive/part-for-whole reckoning; distinguish from speculative three-hour-darkness calculation Augustine discusses then resists

rows.editorialQuestion: Why do the reported post-Resurrection appearances appear in different orders?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: Hence we must examine whether the order which they have put on record
rows.contextGuard: Paul and the Evangelists list overlapping but non-exhaustive manifestations; do not manufacture missing events

rows.editorialQuestion: Does Mark's final appearance occur on Easter evening or toward the Ascension?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: Consequently, in the four evangelists we find mention made of ten distinct appearances
rows.contextGuard: Augustine weighs possibilities and ultimately favors the final meal near the Ascension; source needs complete §§75–77,83

rows.editorialQuestion: Why does the sower sow on rocky ground and among thorns?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: And how can it be reasonable, saith one, to sow among the thorns
rows.contextGuard: Source question is an imagined objection introduced by Chrysostom, not a literal reader question asked historically; rock's capacity to change is central

rows.editorialQuestion: Why do the disciples confidently ask for the tares explanation?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: Whence then arose their confidence in this instance
rows.contextGuard: he appeals to Christ having granted the disciples understanding in private

rows.editorialQuestion: Why ask about the tares rather than leaven or mustard seed?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: And why may it be that they let pass the parable of the leaven
rows.contextGuard: compares the relative clarity of the parables and severity of the tares

rows.editorialQuestion: Why does Christ keep explaining parables privately after the crowds depart?
rows.exactEnglishAnchor: But wherefore doth He still go on, when the others have withdrawn
rows.contextGuard: the homily's explanation concerns the disciples becoming capable of understanding, not an unrestricted claim about every disciple

reuseBasis: Historical 1888 English printed editions and public-domain original scans. CCEL is a work/section locator and secondary transcription witness; prefer original print scans to resolve variant text and missing pages. No permission-request process.
nextResearchStage: Ingest full original printed public-domain source text from authenticated scans/transcriptions, segment by book/homily and section, separate author speech from biblical quotations and modern apparatus, and compute actual overlap against canonical Catena before publication eligibility.
